title: AppState parallel invariant (messages/message_ids/message_senders) documented in struct but not enforced
description: The comment in AppState says 'Push/pop to all three together' and the invariant is documented. However: (1) in handle_state_change there is a push_back to messages BEFORE checking if format_message_line returns Some — the push to message_ids and message_senders only happens inside the if let Some() block, meaning if format_message_line returns None the three deques are NOT pushed together and the invariant would be broken. Reading the code: the messages.push_back(line) is inside the if let Some(line) block (line 808-826 of event.rs). This is actually correct. But the structure is: if let Some(line) = ..., then push to messages, then push to message_ids/senders. A reader unfamiliar with Rust match semantics might think the push happens unconditionally. An assert_eq\!(state.messages.len(), state.message_ids.len()) after each modification site would catch violations during tests.
